scope: Published music identifications and first-person audience reports, excluding the bespoke McFly Enigma song. References are not included in the MP3 count unless a separately verified recording license permits it.

statusKey.fan-identification: Fan archive identification; not a production credit or independently confirmed recording version.
statusKey.audience-report: An audience member names a song; production-wide use and the recording version remain unconfirmed.
statusKey.audience-palette: An eyewitness describes the musical sound but does not identify a track.
statusKey.unresolved-guess: A commenter proposes an identification without corroboration. Do not treat it as established.
statusKey.artist-context: Artist-hosted or first-person context informs programming; it does not establish a show soundtrack.

items.title: Piano Concerto No. 5, Op. 73 — II. Adagio un poco mosso
items.production: Something Wicked This Way Comes; also Trick of the Mind, series 1
items.finding: The fan archive places this calm classical movement beside the blockhead sequence. The exact recording is not identified.
items.programming: Calm music can contrast with an extraordinary physical image; suspense does not always require an ominous beat.

items.title: Unidentified vintage swing with a modern twist
items.finding: June 7 and June 13 audience comments ask about the pre-show tracks; one describes a 1950s swing sound updated for a modern audience. No title is supplied.
items.programming: A welcoming vintage lounge palette for arrival, social mixing, and walk-up.

items.title: Get Happy
items.finding: A viewer reports hearing this song before one performance and explicitly says they do not know whether other performances used the same music.
items.programming: Bright old-showbiz warmth can welcome an audience before the evening becomes strange.

items.title: That's Life
items.production: Showman, televised performance discussed in January 2024
items.finding: A viewer names the song at the ending and asks about the distinctive trumpet outro. Replies do not establish a reliable recording version.
items.programming: A confident, humane walk-off after the last evidence can release a serious scene.

items.title: Unidentified low string passage; Funeral March suggested
items.artist: Unidentified; Chopin is an unverified guess
items.finding: An audience member describes the string atmosphere; a reply guesses Chopin's Funeral March. The guess is not corroborated.
items.programming: Use a restrained string atmosphere if the scene calls for weight; do not label the guess as a confirmed soundtrack cue.

items.title: Unidentified motivational and gospel-organ textures
items.finding: The firsthand account describes motivational music and organ backing but names no recordings.
items.programming: A deliberately framed theatrical scene can use a contrasting gospel or communal palette. It is not a reason to score private testimony.

items.title: The Third Man Theme
items.finding: The fan archive identifies the film theme alongside the Vienna wheel sequence. This is a TV music reference, not evidence of stage use.
items.programming: Place, period, and an unusual instrumental color can give a time-themed scene its identity.

items.title: It's Up to You (Shining Through)
items.finding: The fan archive names this electronic track in its episode music notes. A stage use is not established.
items.programming: A controlled electronic groove can support visible action or arrangement without becoming a reveal sting.

items.title: Can You Feel It
items.finding: The fan archive identifies the recurring song. Its narrative use is more specific than a neutral atmospheric bed.
items.programming: A motif can return with new meaning. Choose an original cue for your own narrative rather than copying the programme's association.

items.title: Die Fledermaus Overture; La Traviata Act I Prelude; Music for the Royal Fireworks Overture; Beethoven Symphony No. 9 finale
items.finding: These are identified as pieces involved in conducting demonstrations, rather than four atmospheric stage beds. They are not counted as additions.
items.programming: Keep routine-content music distinct from incidental scoring.

items.title: Quiet Bach while writing
items.artist: Bach, no work or recording specified
items.production: Derren's description of his writing environment
items.finding: His own blog describes barely audible Bach as part of a writing setup. It does not identify show music.
items.programming: The restrained treatment of concentration beds is our programming inference, not a historical soundtrack claim.

items.title: Inner Circle's intimate table setting
items.artist: Asi Wind; review by Alexis Soloski
items.finding: The artist-hosted review describes a close, conversational card-magic setting but identifies no music tracks.
items.programming: Our ten additions suit intimate interaction and specific effects requested by the owner. They are not presented as music used by Asi.

identificationMethod: The Richard Shakeshaft archive says its music identifications were assembled from fan contributions and ear-based identification. A listing is a useful lead, not a production music credit. See https://www.rmjs.co.uk/derrenbrown/tv.php .
conclusion: The public sources support a handful of named music leads and several palette observations, not 50 verified atmosphere tracks used onstage. The 60 Derren additions are transparently labeled style recommendations. No production-confirmed recording claim is made.
exclusions: The bespoke McFly song used for Enigma's finale
A TVForum Clubbed to Death identification concerns a Newsnight report about a Derren-style character, not a Derren production
Uncorroborated Funeral March guesses are not promoted to confirmed identifications
No specific soundtrack is attributed to Asi Wind without evidence
